title: Authorization boundary model and constrained actor mappings
creator: Anita Rodriguez
description:
Problem: Our current RBAC surface mixes global tenant roles, product-level roles, and ad-hoc resource permissions. That makes it hard to reason about least-privilege, complicates audit trails, and hampers automated rollouts for Dedicated/Private deployments. This ticket designs an RBAC v2 role model that resolves three primary needs: 1) clear resource boundary semantics (resource hierarchy and inheritance), 2) scoped role bindings that support ephemeral/elevated admin workflows, and 3) an auditable permission matrix that maps actions to authorizable artifacts and SSO assertions (SAML/SCIM).

Goals:
- Define a canonical resource hierarchy (Organization > Team > Project > Model/Endpoint > Route/Key) and explain inheritance rules.
- Design scope tokens and binding semantics (resource-scoped, project-scoped, tenant-scoped) with deny-overrides and explicit allow rules.
- Produce a permission matrix that enumerates actions (read, write, serve, manage-config, rotate-keys, escalate) and which roles (operator, viewer, admin, billing, auditor, service-account) can be bound at each scope.
- Specify RBAC primitives (role, role-template, role-binding, attribute constraints) and a compact storage schema for fast evaluation in runtime (O(depth) resolution).
- Define SSO/SAML mapping rules: how assertions map to role-templates, how SCIM provisioning interacts with role bindings, and recommended claims to require (eduPersonPrincipalName or custom claim for org_id).
- Outline audit log schema for RBAC events: binding creation, role changes, breakglass/elevation, policy evaluation failures, and automations that touch bindings.

Non-goals: This ticket is not implementing the runtime evaluator or UI; it focuses on a design and migrations plan that other tickets will implement.
acceptance_criteria: A written resource-hierarchy diagram and inheritance rules document reviewed by Security and Platform teams
Permission matrix spreadsheet enumerating actions and allowed binding scopes for each role-template
SSO mapping section with examples for SAML assertion -> role-template mapping and SCIM sync behavior
Audit schema defined with event types, required fields, and retention notes for Console/Private deployments
Migration plan from RBAC v1 detailing data transformation steps, safe rollouts, and backward compatibility toggles
technical_decisions: Permission tuples will be evaluated as (actor, action, resource, attributes) where attributes are optional constraints (time-bound, IP, tag-constraints)
Inheritance model: downward inheritance with explicit deny override; a deny at any ancestor or explicit deny at resource wins over parent allows
Role-templates are immutable once released; changes produce new role-template versions to make audits deterministic
Storage: store role-bindings as flat records keyed by resource path prefix to allow prefix-scan evaluation in the runtime path
Breakglass/elevation: short-lived ephemeral tokens with audit hooks and mandatory justification stored in audit logs
SSO mapping: prefer a dedicated claim (redwood_roles) populated by IdP for direct bindings; fall back to group -> role-template mapping using SCIM groups
deliverables: Design doc (Confluence): resource hierarchy and permission matrix
Example SAML assertion mapping examples and SCIM provisioning guide
Audit log schema and sample events (JSON) for ingestion to observability pipeline
Migration runbook and SQL/ETL sketch for converting RBAC v1 bindings to RBAC v2
